subject: Streamline discovery: latency & throughput SLOs + procurement roadmap
summary: Post-call recap: customer goals (real-time support scoring), pain (95th pct latency spikes at peak load), proposed SLOs (p95 <120ms, sustained 50 qps), topology options (Dedicated vs Private VPC), PoC scope, and procurement next steps.
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@streamline.ai>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa.procure@streamline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Dec 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Streamline discovery: latency & throughput SLOs + procurement roadmap

Hi Samir / Alyssa —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap so we’re all aligned and to capture the technical asks you flagged: 

1) Business goals (what success looks like)
- Real-time helpdesk scoring: sub-200ms token generation in the critical path for agent suggestions, target 99.9% availability during support hours.
- Cost target: keep per-conversation incremental cost under $0.02/token-equivalent for high-volume channels.

2) Observed pain points
- Current system sees p95 latency spikes up to ~450ms under 2k concurrent chat sessions (your metric).
- KV cache miss rate is significant for session-bound context; this increases overall tokens served.

3) Proposed SLOs for evaluation/PoC
- Latency: p50 <40ms, p90 <85ms, p95 <120ms for 1k qps sustained (per inference endpoint) during business hours.
- Throughput: baseline PoC target = 50 qps sustained per replica; scale to 250 qps with autoscaling and burst pool.
- Availability: 99.9% platform-side during business window; failover to lower-cost regional variant on degradation.

4) Model/quality constraints
- Primary model: 7B instruct-tuned (we recommend quantized INT8 QC profile) for production evaluation.
- Fallback: 3B variant with prompt-tuned safety layer for non-critical channels.
- Token budget: expect ~350 tokens per agent response on average.

5) Deployment topology options (we discussed pros/cons)
- Dedicated (Redwood Dedicated): predictable throughput, isolated GPU pools — easiest to meet p95 targets but higher commit.
- Private VPC (customer-managed infra): required for sensitive PII flows — we support a private control plane with KMS integration.
- Hybrid: Dedicated for high-volume channels + Private VPC for regulated workflows; smart routing by route policy.

6) PoC proposal and success metrics
- 4-week PoC: Week 1 baseline capture + config; Week 2 model tuning/quantization; Week 3 canary at 50 qps; Week 4 scale validation to 250 qps.
- Success: p95 <120ms at 50 qps sustained; KV cache hit >60%; cost per 1k tokens within 15% of our estimate.

7) Procurement and legal asks (Alyssa)
- Streamline will provide standard PO template; Redwood will return a draft SOW + SLA addendum.
- Security intake: we committed to provide SOC 2 evidence snapshots, and a network diagram for the VPC deployment.

Attachments: redwood-slo-estimate-StreamlineAI.pdf (SLO and cost sketch), soc2-evidence-checklist.xlsx, streamline-po-template.docx

Next steps (action items):
- Jordan to send PoC SOW + initial cost sketch (today) — ACTION: Jordan
- Streamline to share PO template and security questionnaire — ACTION: Alyssa
- Rishi/Irene to prepare topology sketch and quantization/perf notes — ACTION: Rishi/Irene (by Monday)

I’ll flag a 30-minute slot for next Tuesday to review the SOW and procurement timeline. If I missed anything, please call it out.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Streamline discovery: latency & throughput SLOs + procurement roadmap — technical notes

Thanks — adding technical detail for the PoC and topology choices so we have a clear internal plan to hand to Streamline: 

1) Benchmarks & expected resource footprint (rough, for PoC)
- Model: 7B int8 quantized (recommended). On A100-class GPU: ~10-12ms per token (in optimal batch), end-to-end approx p95 = kernel + queueing + KV ops ~ 70-100ms at 50 qps with proper batching and KV cache hit >70%.
- Replica sizing: start with 2 replicas for 50 qps (with continuous batching); plan horizontal scale to 6 replicas for 250 qps.
- Memory: KV cache per-replica ~ 8–12GB depending on session window; ensure local NVMe persistence for warm restarts.

2) Caching & batching strategy
- Enable prefix/KV cache for session history; pre-warm top N sessions during canary.
- Adaptive batching: keep max latency cap at 60ms for small requests; fallback to lower batch depth if latency SLO threatened.

3) Routing & fallback
- Primary routing to Dedicated pool (pinned term during PoC). If contention detected, route non-critical traffic to 3B fallback variant in a separate pool.

4) Observability and instrumentation (deliverables)
- Token-level latency breakdown, per-replica queue lengths, KV cache hit/miss metrics, and per-route cost.
- Traces for synthetic replay (Samir will provide) to compare baseline vs Redwood deployment.

5) Security notes for VPC option
- KMS integration for key material; optional HSM for regulatory workflows.
- Network diagram will show private control plane + customer VPC peering + egress rules.

I’ll draft a one-page topology sketch and a short runbook for canary troubleshooting (timeouts, cache warm failures) and attach to the SOW.

— Rishi
